_readme: Hand-read official and press readings for docs/capex.html (DATA_RUNBOOK section 138). Every value was read from the linked document on the 'read' date; amounts in crore unless stated. The government and filings series in docs/capex.json refresh automatically — THIS ledger is updated by hand when RBI (August bulletin), MoSPI (survey / GDP press notes) or a notable press figure publishes.

src.label: RBI Bulletin Aug 2025 — Private Corporate Investment: Growth in 2024-25 and Outlook for 2025-26
Aug 2024 — Growth in 2023-24 and Outlook for 2024-25

rbi.note: Envisaged = ex-ante phasing of project pipelines (Annex Table A4 grand total: banks/FIs + ECB/FCCB/RDB + IPO channels), not realised spending; the most recent year of each article is its outlook. The RBI's headline 'capex envisaged in the coming year' counts only projects already sanctioned (Aug 2025: ₹2,20,132 crore for 2024-25 excluding 2024-25 sanctions vs ₹2,67,432 crore for 2025-26).

rounds.round: CAPEX-2024: Forward-Looking Survey on Private Sector CAPEX Investment Intentions, field work Nov 2024–Jan 2025, published 29 Apr 2025
rounds.note: weighted aggregate for 3,064 responding enterprises (2,368 census + 696 sample; frame 16,025); aggregate capex +66.3% over 2021-22 to 2025-26 per the booklet

rounds.round: CAPEX-2025: second round, field work Oct–Dec 2025, press note Mar 2026
rounds.note: actual 2024-25 capex ₹173.5 crore per enterprise vs ₹180.2 crore intended a year earlier (96.3% realisation); enterprises report the next year cautiously, so 2026-27 intentions understate

src.label: MoSPI press note: Provisional Estimates 2025-26 and Q4 2025-26 (5 Jun 2026)
MoSPI press note: Quarterly estimates Q1 2026-27 (Aug 2026)

gfcf.note: New GDP series, base year 2022-23. Quarterly values are the latest vintage: Q1 2024-25 and Q1 2025-26 as revised in the Aug 2026 note, the rest from the Jun 2026 note. Constant = 2022-23 prices.

press.claim: 341 Nifty 500 companies spent ₹7.61 lakh cr on capex in FY26, nearly double five years ago; operating cash flow ₹11 lakh cr
press.measures: Capex of 341 Nifty 500 companies with a five-year record (the article's own set and definition; paywalled beyond the standfirst)
press.why: Same idea as our Nifty 500 fixed panel (companies with all five years filed). Our set is a different vintage of the index with financials removed, and our capex is PP&E purchases only.

press.claim: Listed non-financial companies' capex reached ₹11 trillion in FY25, outpacing the Centre's ₹10.5 trillion
press.measures: Capex of all listed non-financial companies, FY25 (brokerage aggregation of Capitaline data)
press.why: Same concept. Our store holds fewer small filers and counts PP&E purchases only, so it should sit a little below.

press.claim: Corporate capex +20% y/y in FY25 (public sector +26%, private +18%); 157 companies spent over $100 million
press.measures: Year-on-year growth of the same listed non-financial universe, FY25
press.why: Our same-basis panel grows 10.0% in FY25 (13.9% excluding Reliance, whose PP&E purchases fell 8%). The brokerage's capex definition and company set are not published in the article, so the gap cannot be attributed to one cause.

press.claim: Nifty 50 companies' capex fell 20.7% to ₹5.89 trillion in FY24 from ₹7.43 trillion in FY23 (ex-finance)
press.measures: Gross-block formation — additions to fixed assets in the balance sheet, including capitalised work-in-progress and intangibles such as spectrum
press.why: Different measure: gross-block additions swing with when projects are capitalised (Reliance's 5G roll-out was capitalised in FY23); cash purchases of PP&E do not. On the cash measure the same index rose in FY24.

press.claim: Listed corporates' capex ₹8.5 lakh cr in FY24, ~20% y/y for three years running
press.measures: Capex of listed companies, FY24 (bank research note)
press.why: Same concept; our FY24 same-basis growth is +21.1%, in line with the ~20% they describe.

press.claim: Listed companies projected to invest nearly ₹12.6 lakh cr in FY26
press.measures: Capex of listed companies, FY26 (aggregation not specified)
press.why: Same concept; our total is PP&E purchases by non-financial filers in our store.

press.claim: 168 companies spending more than ₹1,000 cr a year on expansion — highest since 2012
press.measures: Count of listed companies with capex ≥ ₹1,000 cr, FY26
press.why: Same concept; we count non-financial filers only and miss some small/BSE-only filers.

press.claim: Adani group capex ₹1.76 lakh cr in FY26 (₹1.53 lakh cr of 'new investment' per the AGM)
press.measures: Group-wide capex including unlisted arms, acquisitions and intangibles
press.why: We sum PP&E purchases of the listed Adani companies only; the group figure adds unlisted entities and acquisitions (e.g. the NQXT port purchase).

press.claim: Reliance capex ₹1.44 lakh cr in FY26
press.measures: Reliance's reported capex, which includes intangibles (spectrum, software) and capital advances
press.why: Our figure is the cash-flow line 'purchase of property, plant and equipment' only.

press.outlet: CII, as quoted by India Macro Indicators
press.claim: Private capex jumped 67% to ₹7.7 lakh cr in H1 FY26 from ₹4.6 lakh cr a year earlier
press.measures: CII's private-capex series (definition and universe not published in the source)
press.why: The year-ago base matches our half-year cash-flow capex almost exactly (₹4.6 vs ₹4.62 lakh cr) but the H1 FY26 figure does not (₹7.7 vs ₹5.04 lakh cr); without CII's definition the difference cannot be reconciled.

press.claim: Gross fixed assets of 2,383 listed companies grew 5.8% in FY26 to ₹46.7 lakh cr (7.4% in FY25)
press.measures: Balance-sheet stock of gross fixed assets, not the year's spending
press.why: A stock measure (assets on the books) rather than a flow (cash spent in the year); our balance-sheet coverage is also thinner than our cash-flow coverage.

press.claim: Private investment announcements ₹56 lakh cr in FY26 vs ₹37 lakh cr in FY25
press.measures: Value of new projects announced (intentions, multi-year), not spending
press.why: Announcements can take years to become spending and many never do.

press.claim: New private projects announced ₹15.4 lakh cr in Apr–Jun 2026, +97% y/y
press.measures: Project announcements in a quarter (CMIE CapEx database)

press.claim: Private companies invested ₹30.3 trillion in fixed assets in FY25, +7%
press.measures: Gross fixed capital formation of the private corporate sector in the national accounts — listed and unlisted, all asset types incl. intellectual property
press.why: Economy-wide accounts; listed-company cash capex is a subset (ours is about a third of it).

press.claim: Private corporate sector capex ₹11.44 lakh cr in FY26 (provisional); ₹9.55 lakh cr intended for FY27
press.measures: Survey-weighted estimate for the private corporate sector, listed and unlisted
press.why: A survey estimate of a wider population (and a differently weighted second round); shown for scale only.

press.claim: Private capex envisaged at ₹2.67 lakh cr in FY26 vs ₹2.20 lakh cr in FY25 from the project pipeline
press.measures: Ex-ante phasing of projects newly financed by banks/FIs, ECBs and IPOs
press.why: Covers only newly financed projects (a pipeline gauge), not all capex; it is about a quarter of listed-company cash capex.
